investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported that resource as exhausted ("Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption is not applicable to affinity mismatches. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 137–143 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity or configuration failure localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod creation attempt was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: the cluster's 6 nodes have only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, both of which are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for the peer-pod VM workload. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never produced a live agent, so the probe returned no evidence and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (check-expectations.json line 264) was fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported that resource as exhausted ("Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm"), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption is not applicable to affinity mismatches. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 137–143 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity or configuration failure localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the required kata peer-pod VM because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~137–143 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents scheduling layer in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is characterized as an observability eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent — both are unreachable if pod scheduling fails before the agent is live.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing peer-pods, leaving no capacity for new agent pods. Preemption is also blocked, meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free slots.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. This is a compounding constraint — even if global VM capacity existed, only 2 nodes are eligible.

[Medium confidence] Concurrent eval or production workload consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run: the three sibling checks ran sequentially (ending at 12:41, 12:43, 12:46) and each encountered the same exhaustion, suggesting the capacity was not freed between runs.

[Low confidence] A misconfiguration in the kata peer-pods resource limit or node capacity advertisement (e.g., the kata-opa or peer-pods-controller reporting fewer available VM slots than physically available) causing a false exhaustion signal.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not fully consumed, the exhaustion diagnosis would be weakened and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a broken resource advertiser or a pod spec error) would need investigation.

If a manually submitted pod with the same node affinity and kata.peerpods.io/vm resource request schedules successfully immediately after the eval failure, the exhaustion was transient and caused by a concurrent workload spike rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks all pass on the next scheduled eval run without any infrastructure change, the failure was a transient capacity contention event rather than a persistent exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec is found to be misconfigured (e.g., targeting a label that no node currently carries), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a scheduling misconfiguration, and the kata.peerpods.io/vm message would be a secondary symptom.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a subsequent run, the shared scheduling root cause would be disproved and the failure would be localized to the runtime check specifically.

Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 nodes with available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots), alerting on affinity pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.
Add a post-eval cleanup verification step that confirms no kata.peerpods.io/vm-consuming pods from prior eval runs remain in a non-Running state after the withCleanup handler completes.

Add a sibling-correlation eval rule that automatically escalates severity when all checks within a feature (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) fail with the same scheduler message, distinguishing infrastructure-layer failures from application-layer failures.
